# dsh-cot-export
English | 简体中文

Export a DSH session's **complete model chain of thought** — every reasoning
block the model emitted

, turn by turn — to Markdown, JSON, JSONL or plain text,
in one click. The artifact is a normal file

in the workspace, so any other
session, subagent or teammate can read and review it.
Three entry points, one pipeline:
| Entry point | Who calls it |

| Header button **CoT** (beside the session actions) | the user, one click |
| `/cot …` slash comman

d | the user, from the composer |
| `cot_export` / `cot_review` tools | any agent, in any session |

Requirements: DSH **0.2.1-rc.3** (declared compatible in `package.json`) and
Node.js **22.19+ / 24+*

`dsh.compatibility.dshReleases`; the manifest itself i

## What lands on disk

Default location is `<workspace>/cot-exports/`, and every entry point returns
the absolute path.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The Markdown artifact starts with YAML frontmatter (session, workspace, preset,
models, export scope

, counts, and an `exporter: dsh-cot-export@<version>`
provenance stamp) and a `## Index` table that

maps each turn to its line number,
so a reviewer can page through a large export with the built-in `

read` tool
instead of loading it whole.

Reasoning is verbatim. A step that compaction removed from the current model
context is still export

ed (scope `all`) and marked
`> ⚠ superseded — hidden from the current model context by compaction`;

a step
inherited from a fork parent is marked `inherited`.
## Relationship to the built-in session-log export

DSH already ships **Download session log** (Session Header → More) and the
`/export` command (`@deep

seek-ai/dsh-session-log-export`). That is a different
product, not a competitor:
| | Built-in `/export` ZIP | This plugin |
| What you get | The session's **raw event log** as plain `session.vN.jsonl`, every descendant's log
, `media/<attachmentId>.<ext>` images, and `files/<digest>/<name>` uploads | A **derived, readable v

iew** of the same log in five formats |
| Content | Every event: reasoning, tool calls and results,
`system`/`developer` messages, `request/header` tool schemas, compaction, jobs, todos, approvals, co
mmand lifecycle | Reasoning blocks, user prompts, answers, tool calls, and (in HTML/JSON) tool resul

ts; internal events are dropped |
| Size for one real session | 12.3 MB / 3,295 rows / 33 event type

s | 0.8–2.5 MB depending on format |
| Shape | Machine-readable, flat, seq-ordered; needs a decoder

to read comfortably | Organised by turn → step, with an index, anchors and collapsible sections |
|
For agents | No (a browser download) | Yes (`cot_export` / `cot_review` tools, any session) |

Use the built-in export for a **complete archive or forensic copy** — it is the
only thing that carr

ies attachments and byte-exact events. Use this plugin to
**read, review, compare or hand over** the

reasoning. It cannot replace a backup:
attachments, request headers and internal events are not in

annot replace a backup:
attachments, request headers and internal events are not in these artifacts.

session-event-log` in the frontmatter (and the footer of an
HTML artifact) records that distinction.
## Formats
| `format` | File | Shape |
| `markdown` (default) | `.md` | Frontmatter + turn index + one section per turn/step, reasoning fen

ced (the fence adapts when reasoning itself contains backticks) |
| `json` | `.json` | One object: `

{schema, session, exported_at, scope, stats, turns[]}` |
| `jsonl` | `.jsonl` | One object per step

— grep, `jq`, or feed straight into a pipeline |
| `text` | `.txt` | Minimal plain text |
| `html` |
`.html` | Self-contained timeline for browsing: one card per turn, one block per step, collapsible
reasoning/answer/tool results, expand-all buttons, anchors, and a light/dark stylesheet driven by `p
refers-color-scheme`. No external assets, and every piece of session text is HTML-escaped. |

`html` is the replay view: it is the only format that also carries recorded
**tool results** (succes

s/error, arguments, and up to 4000 characters of each
result, marked when truncated), which is what

makes a finished session readable
after the fact without any extra tooling.
## One-click export

Open a session and click the CoT button in the header. One click exports with the
selected format an
d opens a result panel anchored under the button:

- **format** — an explicit segmented control
(`Markdown · HTML · JSON · JSONL · Text`). Picking anot

her format re-exports
immediately and updates the same panel, so the current format is always
visibl

e instead of hidden behind a menu;
- **numbers** — turns, steps, reasoning characters, reasoning tok

he folder the artifact was written to, with **更改** opening the
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy

Reasoning is exported verbatim: it can contain source code, file contents,
paths and secrets the mod

el saw. Artifacts are plaintext files in your
workspace. The plugin makes no network request, sends

nothing anywhere, and
uploads nothing.
